easy.explanation: Proverbs 9:1 says, “Wisdom hath builded her house.”
The verse says that Wisdom hewed out her seven pillars.
easy.q: How many pillars did Wisdom hew out?

easy.explanation: Wisdom calls to the simple and to those who want understanding.

medium.explanation: She killed her beasts, mingled her wine, and furnished her table.
medium.q: What did Wisdom prepare before inviting people?

medium.explanation: Wisdom sent her maidens to cry upon the highest places of the city.
Wisdom calls people to abandon foolishness and go in the way of understanding.
medium.q: What does “Forsake the foolish” mean in this passage?

answers: From the city to the countryside
challenge.explanation: Wisdom calls the simple to forsake foolishness and walk in understanding.
challenge.q: What change does Wisdom seek in the simple person?

challenge.explanation: Wisdom first builds her house, then prepares the meal, and then sends out her invitation.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Wisdom’s actions?

answers: A stable and well-prepared place of wisdom
challenge.explanation: The house and its pillars present Wisdom as established, orderly, and ready to receive guests.
challenge.q: What does the house with seven pillars suggest?

paragraphs.title: Who Benefits from Correction and Wisdom

answers: He hates the one who reproves him
easy.explanation: Proverbs 9:8 says, “Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee.”
easy.q: How does a scorner respond to reproof?

easy.explanation: The passage says to rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.
easy.q: Whom is it wise to reprove?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 9:10 says, “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.”
easy.q: What is the beginning of wisdom?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser.”
medium.q: What happens when instruction is given to a wise man?

medium.explanation: In this context, learning means gaining more knowledge and understanding.
medium.q: What does “learning” mean in “increase in learning”?

answers: Correction can lead to greater wisdom
Correction keeps a person from learning
medium.explanation: The wise and just person receives instruction and increases in wisdom and learning.
medium.q: What is the connection between accepting correction and wisdom?

answers: The scorner accepts it and the wise man rejects it
They respond to it in the same way
The scorner rejects it and the wise man can learn from it
challenge.explanation: The scorner hates reproof, while the wise man receives correction and grows.
challenge.q: What distinguishes the scorner from the wise man regarding correction?

answers: A person himself benefits from choosing wisdom
Only other people benefit from wisdom
Wisdom is unrelated to personal choice
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that a person personally bears the result of his choice.
challenge.q: What does “If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself” teach?

answers: Wisdom can multiply days and increase years
challenge.explanation: Proverbs 9:11 says, “By me thy days shall be multiplied, and the years of thy life shall be increased.”
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between wisdom and life?

paragraphs.title: The Woman of Folly as Wisdom’s Rival

easy.explanation: Proverbs 9:13 says, “A foolish woman is clamorous.”
easy.q: How is the foolish woman described?

answers: At the door of her house
easy.explanation: She sat at the door of her house on a seat in the high places of the city.
easy.q: Where did the foolish woman sit?

easy.explanation: She called passengers who went right on their ways and addressed the simple.

medium.explanation: She is clamorous and calls to people from a visible place in the city.
medium.q: How does the foolish woman try to attract people?

medium.explanation: The word describes someone who makes noise and calls out loudly.
medium.q: What does “clamorous” mean in this passage?

answers: She can be seen and heard by many people
medium.explanation: A high and public place allows her to attract the attention of passers-by.
medium.q: Why does her position in the high places of the city suit her purpose?

answers: As a rival offering a competing call
challenge.explanation: The foolish woman calls to the simple in a way that contrasts with Wisdom’s invitation.
challenge.q: How is the foolish woman presented in relation to Wisdom?

answers: They compete for the attention of passers-by
Both work only inside their houses
challenge.explanation: Both voices are presented publicly, but they offer opposing paths.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from both Wisdom and Folly calling from prominent places in the city?

challenge.explanation: She addresses the simple and those who lack understanding.
challenge.q: What detail identifies the foolish woman’s audience?

paragraphs.title: The Sweetness of Sin and Its End

easy.q: What does Folly describe as sweet?

easy.explanation: The verse says that bread eaten in secret is pleasant.
easy.q: What is pleasant according to Folly?

answers: To the dead and the depths of hell
easy.explanation: The passage reveals that the dead are there and that her guests are in the depths of hell.
easy.q: Where does Folly’s invitation ultimately lead?

answers: They present stolen and hidden things as sweet and pleasant
They invite him to study wisdom
medium.explanation: Folly describes stolen waters and secret bread as desirable.
medium.q: Why do Folly’s words tempt a person?

medium.explanation: The phrase presents something secret and sinful as an attractive pleasure.
medium.q: What does “bread eaten in secret” suggest?

answers: That the invitation leads to a dangerous end
medium.explanation: He does not know that the dead and the depths of hell are there.
medium.q: What does the simple person fail to know?

answers: It appears sweet and pleasant but leads to death
It appears dangerous but leads to wisdom
It appears hidden but leads to fame
challenge.explanation: Folly makes sin seem pleasant, but the passage shows that its end is death and hell.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the appearance of the temptation and its end?

answers: They show that the temptation involves hidden and forbidden things
They prove that it is a public feast
They describe the way of understanding
challenge.explanation: These words reveal both the secrecy and the wrongness of the temptation.
challenge.q: Why are the words “stolen” and “secret” important?

answers: They show that something pleasant at first may end in hell
They teach that everything sweet is wisdom
They say that pleasant things are always openly dangerous
challenge.explanation: The invitation feels pleasant, but its hidden result is deadly.
challenge.q: How do these verses warn against relying only on pleasant feelings?
